def policy_source():
    return (POLICY_SOURCE.replace('FRAME_MAGIC_VALUE', str(FRAME_MAGIC))
            .replace('RESPONSE_MAGIC_VALUE', str(RESPONSE_MAGIC))
            .replace('PATH_PREFIX_FIRST', str(int.from_bytes(b'/proc/se', 'little')))
            .replace('PATH_PREFIX_SECOND', str(int.from_bytes(b'lf/fd/', 'little'))))


def _parts():
    text = bytearray(BRIDGE)
    struct.pack_into('<i', text, POLICY_HOLE, len(text) - POLICY_HOLE - 4)
    names = ['', '_start', *IMPORTS]
    strings = bytearray(b'\0')
    positions = {'': 0}
    for name in names[1:]:
        positions[name] = len(strings)
        strings.extend(name.encode('ascii') + b'\0')
    symbols = [bytes(24), struct.pack('<IBBHQQ', 0, 3, 0, 1, 0, 0),
               struct.pack('<IBBHQQ', positions['_start'], 18, 0, 1, 0, START_SIZE)]
    symbol_at = {'_start': 2}
    for name in IMPORTS:
        symbol_at[name] = len(symbols)
        symbols.append(struct.pack('<IBBHQQ', positions[name], 18, 0, 0, 0, 0))
    relas = b''.join(struct.pack('<QQq', at, (symbol_at[name] << 32) | 4, -4)
                     for at, name in BRIDGE_RELOCATIONS)
    section_strings = b'\0.text\0.rela.text\0.symtab\0.strtab\0.shstrtab\0.note.GNU-stack\0'
    return bytes(text), relas, b''.join(symbols), bytes(strings), section_strings


def _header(section_offset):
    return struct.pack('<16sHHIQQQIHHHHHH', b'\x7fELF\x02\x01\x01' + bytes(9),
                       1, 62, 1, 0, 0, section_offset, 0, 64, 0, 0, 64, 7, 5)


def _sections(policy, rela_at, symbols_at, strings_at, shstrings_at, stack_at):
    text, relas, symbols, strings, section_strings = _parts()
    name = {key: section_strings.index(key.encode() + b'\0')
            for key in ('.text', '.rela.text', '.symtab', '.strtab', '.shstrtab', '.note.GNU-stack')}
    rows = [
        bytes(64),
        struct.pack('<IIQQQQIIQQ', name['.text'], 1, 6, 0, 64, len(text)+policy, 0, 0, 16, 0),
        struct.pack('<IIQQQQIIQQ', name['.rela.text'], 4, 64, 0, rela_at, len(relas), 3, 1, 8, 24),
        struct.pack('<IIQQQQIIQQ', name['.symtab'], 2, 0, 0, symbols_at, len(symbols), 4, 2, 8, 24),
        struct.pack('<IIQQQQIIQQ', name['.strtab'], 3, 0, 0, strings_at, len(strings), 0, 0, 1, 0),
        struct.pack('<IIQQQQIIQQ', name['.shstrtab'], 3, 0, 0, shstrings_at, len(section_strings), 0, 0, 1, 0),
        struct.pack('<IIQQQQIIQQ', name['.note.GNU-stack'], 1, 0, 0, stack_at, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0),
    ]
    return b''.join(rows)


def reference_object(policy):
    'Independent struct-based whole-object representation for actual bytes.'
    if type(policy) is not bytes or not policy or len(policy) > 1 << 20:
        raise ValueError('nonempty bounded actual policy image required')
    text, relas, symbols, strings, section_strings = _parts()
    raw = bytearray(bytes(64) + text + policy)
    raw.extend(bytes((-len(raw)) % 8))
    rela_at = len(raw); raw.extend(relas)
    symbols_at = len(raw); raw.extend(symbols)
    strings_at = len(raw); raw.extend(strings)
    shstrings_at = len(raw); raw.extend(section_strings)
    stack_at = len(raw)
    raw.extend(bytes((-len(raw)) % 8))
    section_offset = len(raw)
    raw.extend(_sections(len(policy), rela_at, symbols_at, strings_at, shstrings_at, stack_at))
    if len(raw) > 1 << 20:
        raise ValueError('observer object exceeds existing one MiB output capacity')
    raw[:64] = _header(section_offset)
    return bytes(raw)


def packer_source():
    text, relas, symbols, strings, section_strings = _parts()
    parts = [('prefix', _header(0) + text),
             ('tail', relas + symbols + strings + section_strings),
             ('sections', _sections(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0))]
    functions = []
    calls = {}
    for name, data in parts:
        names = []
        for group, begin in enumerate(range(0, len(data), 48 * 8)):
            function = f'emit_{name}_{group}'
            names.append(function)
            lines = [f'def {function}(o:mutbuf, base:u64) -> u64:']
            for at in range(begin, min(begin + 48 * 8, len(data)), 8):
                chunk = data[at:at+8]
                if any(chunk):
                    lines.append(f'    write(o, base + {at}, {int.from_bytes(chunk,"little")}, {len(chunk)})')
            lines.append('    return 0')
            functions.append('\n'.join(lines))
        calls[name] = names
    result = f'''def pack(s:readbuf, o:mutbuf, w:mutbuf) -> u32:
    policy = length(s)
    if policy == 0 or policy > 1048576:
        return 4294967295
    relas = ({64+len(text)} + policy + 7) & 18446744073709551608
    symbols = relas + {len(relas)}
    strings = symbols + {len(symbols)}
    shstrings = strings + {len(strings)}
    stack = shstrings + {len(section_strings)}
    sections = (stack + 7) & 18446744073709551608
    size = sections + 448
    if size > 1048576 or length(o) < size:
        return 4294967294
    i = 0
    while i < size:
        store(o, i, 0)
        i = i + 1
'''
    for key, base in (('prefix','0'), ('tail','relas'), ('sections','sections')):
        for function in calls[key]:
            result += f'    {function}(o, {base})\n'
    result += f'''    write(o, 40, sections, 8)
    write(o, sections + 96, {len(text)} + policy, 8)
    write(o, sections + 152, relas, 8)
    write(o, sections + 216, symbols, 8)
    write(o, sections + 280, strings, 8)
    write(o, sections + 344, shstrings, 8)
    write(o, sections + 408, stack, 8)
    i = 0
    while i < policy:
        store(o, {64+len(text)} + i, byte(s, i))
        i = i + 1
    return size
'''
    return result + '\n\n' + '\n\n'.join(functions) + POLICY_SOURCE[POLICY_SOURCE.index('\ndef write('):]


def assembled_bridge():
    'Assemble the independent oracle only in source tests, never building.'
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='hia-linked-observer-reference-') as folder:
        obj = Path(folder)/'reference.o'
        subprocess.run(['as','--64',str(ROOT/'tools/hia_linked_observer_bridge.S'),'-o',str(obj)],
                       check=True,capture_output=True,timeout=30)
        raw = obj.read_bytes()
    header = struct.unpack_from('<16sHHIQQQIHHHHHH',raw)
    rows = [struct.unpack_from('<IIQQQQIIQQ',raw,header[6]+i*header[11]) for i in range(header[12])]
    r = rows[header[13]]; names = raw[r[4]:r[4]+r[5]]
    def string(data,at): return data[at:data.index(0,at)].decode('ascii')
    named = {string(names,r[0]):r for r in rows}
    text = named['.text']; table = named['.symtab']; r = rows[table[6]]
    strings = raw[r[4]:r[4]+r[5]]
    symbols = [struct.unpack_from('<IBBHQQ',raw,table[4]+i) for i in range(0,table[5],24)]
    values = {string(strings,row[0]):row for row in symbols}
    relas = []
    for row in rows:
        if row[1] == 4 and rows[row[7]] == text:
            for i in range(0,row[5],24):
                at,info,addend = struct.unpack_from('<QQq',raw,row[4]+i)
                if info & 0xffffffff != 4 or addend != -4:
                    raise AssertionError('foreign relocation representation differs')
                relas.append((at,string(strings,symbols[info>>32][0])))
    return (raw[text[4]:text[4]+text[5]],tuple(relas),values['policy_hole'][4],values['_start'][5])


def main():
    for name, source in (('linked_observer_policy',policy_source()), ('linked_observer_packer',packer_source())):
        path = ROOT/'examples/hia_bootstrap'/f'{name}.hiaasm'
        path.write_text(render_assembly(document(source,name)))
        print(path.name,path.stat().st_size)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

"""Native transport for linked self-host qualification, with the real ELF loader.

Each call execs a fresh HIA-policy-directed adapter, dlopens the exact complete sealed
target shared object, and calls its fixed byte ABI. This helper does not replace
the independent seed/shared loader, parse HIA, compile user code, reuse a child,
or claim a security sandbox. It is selected only for the qualifier's linked HIA
objects. Non-whitespace private response noise is refused, never searched for a
later magic sequence; the original JSON loader's boundary whitespace is kept.

The real libc startup/exit path preserves loader constructors/finalizers.
Reported values and ordinary output are captured before normal finalization;
requested trap/shared-output observation reads the actual mapping after exit.
A separate parent-owned snapshot is committed by the native observer after f0,
before publishing stdout or entering libc exit. It retains ordinary output even
when a finalizer traps, exits nonzero, or prevents a well-formed stdout report.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from contextlib import contextmanager
import fcntl
from hashlib import sha256
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import time

from tools.hia_selfhost_native_observer import (LIMIT, WORKSPACE_FIELDS, digest,
                                               frame, shared_output, read_capture)

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
POLICY = ROOT / "examples/hia_bootstrap/linked_observer_policy.hiaasm"
PACKER = ROOT / "examples/hia_bootstrap/linked_observer_packer.hiaasm"
SOURCE_PATHS = (POLICY, PACKER, ROOT / "tools/generate_hia_linked_observer.py",
                ROOT / "tools/hia_linked_observer_bridge.S")


def _vm(checked, source, output, workspace):
    # Public admission precedes the actual finite Core interpreter. Its scalar
    # return wrapper cannot expose a complete ELF at once; observe the actual
    # three owned buffers, without replacing the program's writes by a hash.
    from hepta.hia_program_runtime import _Machine, _Owner, _View
    owners = [_Owner(i+1, bytearray(raw)) for i, raw in enumerate((source, output, workspace))]
    machine = _Machine(checked, 30_000_000, 4 << 20, None, 128)
    values = machine.invoke(machine.functions['f0'],
                            [_View(owner, i != 0) for i, owner in enumerate(owners)])
    if bytes(owners[0].data) != source:
        raise AssertionError('linked observer VM changed immutable input')
    return values, bytes(owners[1].data), bytes(owners[2].data), machine.steps


def source_identity():
    return {p.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix(): digest(p.read_bytes()) for p in SOURCE_PATHS}


def vm_packer(checked, policy):
    from tools.generate_hia_linked_observer import reference_object
    expected = reference_object(policy)
    values, output, workspace, steps = _vm(checked, policy, b'\xa5'*len(expected), b'')
    if values != [len(expected)] or output != expected or workspace:
        raise AssertionError('linked observer VM did not reproduce every actual object byte')
    return output, {'input_bytes':len(policy),'input_sha256':digest(policy),
                    'output_bytes':len(output),'output_sha256':digest(output),
                    'result':values,'steps':steps,'every_output_byte_compared':True}


def independent_reference(*, before_B0=False):
    """All continuation actions and complete object bytes precede compilation."""
    from hepta.hia_agent_assembly import assemble_program
    before = source_identity()
    policy = assemble_program(POLICY.read_bytes())
    packer = assemble_program(PACKER.read_bytes())
    packing = []
    for actual in (b'\xc3', bytes(range(256))*17):
        _, receipt = vm_packer(packer, actual)
        packing.append(receipt)
    workspace, control = bytearray(512), bytes(512)
    struct.pack_into('<Q', workspace, 8, 1)
    request = _linked_frame(b'complete ELF remains opaque to policy',b'source\0\xff',17,40,90,None,11)
    observations = []
    def step(source, expected, feedback=()):
        nonlocal workspace, control
        for at, value in feedback:
            struct.pack_into('<Q',workspace,at,value)
        values, control, updated, steps = _vm(policy,source,control,bytes(workspace))
        workspace = bytearray(updated)
        if values != [expected]:
            raise AssertionError('linked observer VM continuation differs')
        observations.append({'action':expected,'output_hex':control.hex(),
                             'workspace_hex':updated.hex(),'steps':steps})
        return control
    first = step(b'',1)
    if struct.unpack_from('<8Q',first) != (5242937,10,256<<20,8<<20,16<<20,32,0,0):
        raise AssertionError('linked observer resource limits differ')
    step(request,2,((16,0),))
    path = step(request,3,((16,0),(24,7),(32,15)))

def _runtime_interpreter():
    """Read only the admitted running interpreter's ELF representation."""
    executable = Path(sys.executable).resolve(strict=True)
    data = executable.read_bytes()
    if len(data) < 64 or data[:7] != b"\x7fELF\x02\x01\x01":
        raise ValueError("linked observer requires the actual Linux x86-64 ELF interpreter")
    fields = struct.unpack_from("<16sHHIQQQIHHHHHH", data)
    _, kind, machine, version, _, phoff, _, _, ehsize, phsize, phnum, _, _, _ = fields
    if kind not in (2, 3) or machine != 62 or version != 1 or ehsize != 64 or phsize != 56:
        raise ValueError("running interpreter has an unsupported ELF representation")
    if phoff > len(data) or phnum > (len(data) - phoff) // phsize:
        raise ValueError("running interpreter program headers are outside the file")
    interpreters = []
    for index in range(phnum):
        header = struct.unpack_from("<IIQQQQQQ", data, phoff + index * phsize)
        if header[0] == 3:
            offset, size = header[2], header[5]
            if offset > len(data) or size > len(data) - offset:
                raise ValueError("running interpreter PT_INTERP is outside the file")
            raw = data[offset:offset + size]
            if not raw.startswith(b"/") or not raw.endswith(b"\0") or b"\0" in raw[:-1]:
                raise ValueError("running interpreter PT_INTERP is not one absolute path")
            interpreters.append(os.fsdecode(raw[:-1]))
    if len(interpreters) != 1:
        raise ValueError("running interpreter must identify exactly one system loader")
    path = Path(interpreters[0])
    raw = path.read_bytes()
    return path, {"executable": str(executable), "executable_sha256": digest(data),
                  "interpreter": str(path), "resolved_interpreter": str(path.resolve(strict=True)),
                  "interpreter_sha256": digest(raw)}


def execute(executable_bytes, request, *, cwd, timeout=20, arguments=(), output_fd=None, snapshot_fd=None):
    """Exec exact sealed bytes, with binary stdin/stdout; never interpret them."""
    fd = os.memfd_create('hia-linked-native-observer', os.MFD_ALLOW_SEALING)
    try:
        view = memoryview(executable_bytes)
        while view:
            written = os.write(fd, view)
            if written <= 0:
                raise OSError('short observer image write')
            view = view[written:]
        fcntl.fcntl(fd, getattr(fcntl,'F_ADD_SEALS',1033), 15)
        if fcntl.fcntl(fd, getattr(fcntl,'F_GET_SEALS',1034)) & 15 != 15:
            raise OSError('observer image sealing failed')
        return subprocess.run(['/proc/self/fd/'+str(fd), *arguments], input=request,
            cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, timeout=timeout, pass_fds=(fd, *(value for value in (output_fd, snapshot_fd) if value is not None)),
            env=None)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


@contextmanager
def output_snapshot(capacity):
    """Own a fixed-size return snapshot, separate from the live output mapping."""
    if type(capacity) is not int or not 0 <= capacity <= LIMIT:
        raise ValueError('native output snapshot exceeds the unchanged byte ABI limit')
    descriptor = os.memfd_create('hia-linked-return-snapshot', os.MFD_ALLOW_SEALING)
    try:
        # Fresh anonymous pages include a zero completion word. The snapshot
        # may be filled, but its shape cannot be changed by the child.
        os.ftruncate(descriptor, 8 + capacity)
        fcntl.fcntl(descriptor, getattr(fcntl, 'F_ADD_SEALS', 1033), 7)
        if fcntl.fcntl(descriptor, getattr(fcntl, 'F_GET_SEALS', 1034)) & 7 != 7:
            raise OSError('return snapshot extent sealing failed')
        yield descriptor
    finally:
        os.close(descriptor)


def _linked_frame(image, source, capacity, workspace_size, workspace_fill,
                  output_fd, snapshot_fd):
    original = frame(image, source, capacity, workspace_size, workspace_fill, output_fd)
    if (type(snapshot_fd) is not int or not 3 <= snapshot_fd <= 2147483647
            or snapshot_fd == output_fd):
        raise ValueError('native return snapshot descriptor is invalid')
    descriptors = struct.pack('<2I', 0xffffffff if output_fd is None else output_fd, snapshot_fd)
    return b'HIAOBS03' + original[8:48] + descriptors + original[56:]


def read_output_snapshot(descriptor, capacity):
    marker = os.pread(descriptor, 8, 0)
    if len(marker) != 8:
        raise OSError('short native return completion word')
    completed = int.from_bytes(marker, 'little')
    if completed == 0:
        return None
    if completed != capacity + 1:
        raise ValueError('native return snapshot completion differs')
    result = bytearray()
    while len(result) < capacity:
        part = os.pread(descriptor, capacity - len(result), 8 + len(result))
        if not part:
            raise OSError('short native return snapshot')
        result.extend(part)
    return bytes(result)


def _response_frame(raw, expected):
    """Keep the old JSON loader's boundary whitespace without trimming buffers.

    Only JSON's four ASCII whitespace bytes may precede the first magic byte
    or follow the complete fixed-length response. The frame itself, including
    trailing whitespace in source/output/workspace, is copied without changes.
    A later magic sequence is never searched for.
    """
    begin = 0
    while begin < len(raw) and raw[begin] in b" \t\r\n":
        begin += 1
    end = begin + expected
    if end > len(raw) or raw[begin:begin + 8] != b"HIAOBR03":
        return None
    for byte in raw[end:]:
        if byte not in b" \t\r\n":
            return None
    return raw[begin:end]

def digest(data):
    return sha256(data).hexdigest()


def elf_contents(data):
    header=struct.unpack_from("<16sHHIQQQIHHHHHH",data)
    if header[0][:7]!=b"\x7fELF\x02\x01\x01" or header[2]!=62:
        raise AssertionError("expected the actual ELF64 x86-64 artifact")
    rows=[struct.unpack_from("<IIQQQQIIQQ",data,header[6]+index*header[11])
          for index in range(header[12])]
    name_row=rows[header[13]]
    names=data[name_row[4]:name_row[4]+name_row[5]]
    def string(raw,at):
        end=raw.index(0,at)
        return raw[at:end].decode("ascii")
    named={string(names,row[0]):row for row in rows}
    text=named[".text"]
    sym=named[".symtab"]; strings=rows[sym[6]]
    strings=data[strings[4]:strings[4]+strings[5]]
    symbols=[struct.unpack_from("<IBBHQQ",data,sym[4]+at)
             for at in range(0,sym[5],sym[9])]
    symbols=[{"name":string(strings,row[0]),"binding":row[1]>>4,"kind":row[1]&15,
              "section":row[3],"value":row[4],"size":row[5]} for row in symbols]
    relas=[]
    for row in rows:
        if row[1]==4 and rows[row[7]]==text:
            for at in range(0,row[5],row[9]):
                offset,info,addend=struct.unpack_from("<QQq",data,row[4]+at)
                relas.append((offset,info&0xffffffff,symbols[info>>32]["name"],addend))
    return {"text":data[text[4]:text[4]+text[5]],"relocations":relas,
            "symbols":symbols,"sections":named}

def seal_errno_filter():
    """Install a child-only extra restriction; never enable ptrace or relax policy."""
    import ctypes
    class Filter(ctypes.Structure):
        _fields_=[("code",ctypes.c_ushort),("jt",ctypes.c_ubyte),
                  ("jf",ctypes.c_ubyte),("k",ctypes.c_uint32)]
    class Program(ctypes.Structure):
        _fields_=[("len",ctypes.c_ushort),("filter",ctypes.POINTER(Filter))]
    # seccomp_data: arch at4, syscall nr at0, argument1 at24.
    # Keep every other x86-64 syscall under the process's inherited restrictions.
    instructions=((0x20,0,0,4),(0x15,1,0,0xc000003e),(0x06,0,0,0x80000000),
                  (0x20,0,0,0),(0x15,0,3,72),(0x20,0,0,24),(0x15,0,1,1034),
                  (0x06,0,0,0x00050001),(0x06,0,0,0x7fff0000))
    code=(Filter*len(instructions))(*(Filter(*row) for row in instructions))
    program=Program(len(code),code)
    libc=ctypes.CDLL(None,use_errno=True)
    prctl=libc.prctl;prctl.restype=ctypes.c_int
    prctl.argtypes=[ctypes.c_int,ctypes.c_ulong,ctypes.c_void_p,
                   ctypes.c_ulong,ctypes.c_ulong]
    def install():
        if prctl(38,1,None,0,0)!=0:
            raise OSError(ctypes.get_errno(),"PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS")
        if prctl(22,2,ctypes.byref(program),0,0)!=0:
            raise OSError(ctypes.get_errno(),"PR_SET_SECCOMP")
    return install,{"instructions":instructions,"bytes":bytes(code).hex(),
        "restriction":"x86-64 fcntl syscall72 command1034 returns EPERM",
        "other_syscalls":"inherited kernel restrictions unchanged",
        "ptrace_requested":False}

# HIA policy for fresh linked ELF observations

This component replaces the per-call Python loader used by the self-host
qualifier's selected `linked-selfhost` phases. Each observation still execs a
fresh process, loads the complete original sealed shared object through the
real system dynamic loader, and calls its existing six-word byte ABI. The HIA
policy owns the request checks, exact resource-limit values, continuation
sequence, response header, snapshot permission, and final status. Fixed
Linux/SysV transport performs the requested foreign operations.

This is component development, not whole-source cold qualification, default
activation, proof for every foreign DSO, or authorization to delete the retained
loader. The independent `seed-shared` path, B0 trust boundary, generation
controls, and retained reference loader remain explicit dependencies. Whole
native, default, live migration, and legacy deletion flags remain false.

## One selected route

The qualifier uses `NATIVE_LINKED_OBSERVER`, phase input `linked_observer`, and
the exact `linked-observer.elf` produced by this candidate. Every phase manifest
binds the executable's current bytes and checks them before selecting it.
Selection is explicit for `linked-selfhost`; a selected missing or invalid
observer raises or refuses and never falls back to the Python loader. The
published general observer `invoke(..., image_format="linked-selfhost")`
delegates to the same implementation.

`tools/generate_hia_linked_observer.py` authors two checked HIA sources:

* `linked_observer_policy.hiaasm` contains the continuation state machine.
* `linked_observer_packer.hiaasm` receives the actual newly compiled policy
  image and emits every byte of a complete ELF64 x86-64 relocatable object.

The packer includes the full policy image in the executable text. It does not
substitute a digest or a prebuilt policy. The real system `ld` then resolves
the observer's fixed `__libc_start_main`, `dlopen`, `dlsym`, `dlerror`, and `exit`
imports. The interpreter path comes from the running interpreter's real ELF
`PT_INTERP`, whose bytes are bound before and after construction. No target
`.text` section is extracted as a replacement for shared-object loading.

The fixed bridge is independently described in
`tools/hia_linked_observer_bridge.S`. This is an authoring and test oracle;
construction does not run an assembler or read that file. Its complete machine
bytes and external relocation sites are checked against an actual GNU
assembler. HIA emits the whole object, and an independent ordinary Core VM
checks every emitted byte for synthetic policy inputs and the actual newly
compiled policy image.

## HIA and foreign mechanism boundary

The fixed bridge contains action dispatch and the mechanics of read, write,
mmap, sealing, time measurement, and calls through the system loader. It
returns the actual foreign values to HIA. It has no implementation of the
request-field limits or of the decision to call, commit, publish, or finish.
It reports bridge allocation/dispatch failures as the private transport
failure status. Kernel errno handling and short-write loops are physical
transport, not a replacement policy.

The HIA workspace and control buffers are each exactly 512 bytes. Workspace
word zero selects the next phase. Words at 16 through 56 carry actual foreign
feedback. HIA retains admitted request fields at 64 through 112. The ordinary
successful action sequence is:

| Action | Foreign operation authorized by HIA |
|---|---|
| 1 | Apply original process limits and read one complete request |
| 2 | Create, fill, and seal the complete target shared image |
| 3 | `dlopen` the actual owned descriptor with `RTLD_LOCAL | RTLD_NOW` |
| 4 | Resolve `f0`, then close the owned image descriptor |
| 5 | Prepare source, output, and workspace ABI storage |
| 6 | Measure and call the actual entry point |
| 8 | Write the ordinary return snapshot and then its completion marker |
| 7 | Publish the HIA-created header and complete ABI postimages |
| 0 | Enter actual libc exit with the HIA-selected status |

Action 9 obtains the real loader diagnostic after a failed lookup; its
continuation selects the final refusal. Successful completion never requests
an eager `dlclose`. Actual native policy tests compare each returned action,
the complete output buffer, the complete workspace, readonly input, and
surrounding canaries with the independent retained Core interpreter. Refusal
controls cover phase, feedback, framing, descriptors, and short state/output
storage, including negative errno values.

## Exact limits and input protocol

The previous byte ABI limits are unchanged: a nonempty target image no larger
than 4 MiB, source/output/workspace each no larger than 1 MiB, and a fill byte
from 0 through 255. The child keeps the original 20-second wall supervision,
10-second CPU limit, 256 MiB address-space limit, 8 MiB stack limit, 16 MiB file
limit, 32 descriptors, zero core limit, and nondumpable state. Every child is a
fresh exec; no successor process or loaded image is reused.

The private `HIAOBS03` request retains the 56-byte header. The last word holds
two transport-owned 32-bit descriptors: the optional live-output descriptor
(`0xffffffff` means absent) and the mandatory return-snapshot descriptor.
HIA validates their ranges and rejects collision. These descriptors are not
chosen by the target source. The complete original target bytes and source
bytes follow the header; length must be exact. The request read arena has
one extra byte so HIA can distinguish the unchanged admitted maximum from an
oversized request. No general Core-language or compiler-profile limit is
changed by this component.

## Target lifetime and two output observations

The observer enters through libc startup and registers the actual runtime
loader finalizer. The target remains loaded until actual process exit.
Constructors, process exit callbacks, finalizers, their stdout/stderr writes,
nonzero exits, and signals remain real foreign effects. A failed `dlsym`
after a successful constructor still reaches libc finalization. There is no
signal conversion or suppression of a target finalizer.

The original loader captures an ordinary return before finalization. A
finalizer can then alter a requested shared output mapping or exit
abnormally. These are two different observations and the implementation
keeps both:

* A parent-owned fixed-size snapshot memfd contains `8 + capacity` bytes.
  HIA authorizes its fill only after `f0` and the ending clock have returned.
  Native transport writes all output bytes before a `capacity + 1` completion
  word. A zero word means no completed call; marker one represents a
  completed zero-length output. A constructor's fabricated stdout frame
  cannot invent this completion.
* The optional live output mapping remains the actual shared map. When
  `observe_trap_writes` is requested, the parent reads it after process
  termination, including real finalizer writes. Otherwise ordinary output
  comes from the committed pre-finalizer snapshot, even if a later finalizer
  exits nonzero, traps, or prevents a valid stdout response.

All descriptors are explicitly retained through their required lifetime and
closed on prelaunch failures and normal/refused completion. The tests include
failure of the second parent-owned allocation while the first descriptor is
live. The bridge is a fixed foreign ABI mechanism, not an isolation boundary
against malicious native code in the same child.

## Output framing preserves original JSON boundary whitespace

`HIAOBR03` has a 24-byte header followed by exact source, output, and workspace
bytes. The host materializer accepts only the original JSON parser's four
ASCII whitespace bytes before the first magic byte and after the complete
fixed-size frame. It does not search for later magic, accept arbitrary noise,
strip payload bytes, or remove whitespace at the end of a legitimate binary
buffer. Successful stderr output remains allowed. Both response output and
committed snapshot must agree before a successful observation is reported.

The qualifier executes independent policy and packer VM observations before

No original check or deadline is removed to obtain a result.

The component fixture has mutually exclusive matching-source cold and

Development uses the actual supplied retained bytes and labels its scope;

def digest(data):

def independent_reference():
    """VM executes the actual HIA ELF packer, before any B0 is generated."""
    from hepta.hia_agent_assembly import assemble_program
    from hepta.hia_program import execute_program
    from tools.generate_hia_native_observer import reference_image
    image = reference_image()
    from tools.hia_selfhost_bulk import Body
    observations = []
    # The Core ABI has a bounded return list. Observe disjoint windows from
    # fresh executions, covering EVERY byte without hashes standing for data.
    for begin in range(0,len(image),128):
        end = min(begin+128,len(image))
        body = Body(0); owners=[]; views=[]
        for count in (0,len(image),0):
            owner=body.value('buffer','buffer.new',[body.const('usize',count)])
            view=body.value('mutbuf','borrow.mut',[owner])
            owners.append(owner);views.append(view)
        body.effect('buffer.fill',[views[1],body.const('u8',165)])
        body.effect('loan.end',[views[0]])
        views[0]=body.value('readbuf','borrow.read',[owners[0]])
        result=body.value('u32','call',views,{'function':'f0'})
        values=[result]+[body.value('u8','buffer.load',[views[1],body.const('usize',at)])
                        for at in range(begin,end)]
        for view in views:body.effect('loan.end',[view])
        for owner in owners:body.effect('owner.drop',[owner])
        returns=','.join(['u32']+['u8']*(end-begin))
        wrapper=('hia-asm.v1 hepta.hia.program.v8 observer_reference\n'
            +'fn reference_entry() -> ('+returns+') effects(alloc,read,write,trap) entry(b0)\n'
            +'block b0()\n'+body.text()+'  ret('+','.join(values)+')\nend\n'

        if observed.get('status')!='returned' or observed['values']!=[len(image),*image[begin:end]]:
            raise AssertionError('independent VM did not reproduce exact observer ELF window')
        observations.append({'begin':begin,'end':end,'vm_core_sha256':checked.sha256,'result':observed})
    return {'before_B0':True, 'packer_source_sha256':digest(PACKER.read_bytes()),

def frame(image, source, capacity, workspace_size, workspace_fill, output_fd=None):
    if (not isinstance(image, bytes) or not 0 < len(image) <= 4*LIMIT
            or not isinstance(source, bytes) or len(source) > LIMIT
            or type(capacity) is not int or not 0 <= capacity <= LIMIT
            or type(workspace_size) is not int or not 0 <= workspace_size <= LIMIT
            or type(workspace_fill) is not int or not 0 <= workspace_fill <= 255
            or (output_fd is not None and (type(output_fd) is not int or not 3 <= output_fd <= 2147483647))):
        raise ValueError('native observer frame exceeds the unchanged byte ABI limits')
    return b'HIAOBS02'+struct.pack('<6Q',len(image),len(source),capacity,workspace_size,workspace_fill,
        (1<<64)-1 if output_fd is None else output_fd)+image+source


def execute(executable_bytes, request, *, cwd, timeout=20, arguments=(), output_fd=None):
    """Exec exact sealed bytes, with binary stdin/stdout; never interpret them."""
    fd = os.memfd_create('hia-native-observer', os.MFD_ALLOW_SEALING)
    try:
        view = memoryview(executable_bytes)
        while view:
            written = os.write(fd, view)
            if written <= 0:
                raise OSError('short observer image write')
            view = view[written:]
        fcntl.fcntl(fd, getattr(fcntl,'F_ADD_SEALS',1033), 15)
        if fcntl.fcntl(fd, getattr(fcntl,'F_GET_SEALS',1034)) & 15 != 15:
            raise OSError('observer image sealing failed')
        return subprocess.run(['/proc/self/fd/'+str(fd), *arguments], input=request,
            cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, timeout=timeout, pass_fds=(fd,) if output_fd is None else (fd,output_fd),
            env={'PATH':'/usr/bin:/bin','LANG':'C.UTF-8','LC_ALL':'C.UTF-8','TZ':'UTC'})
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


@contextmanager
def shared_output(initial, enabled):
    if not enabled:
        yield None
        return
    descriptor=os.memfd_create('hia-native-output',os.MFD_ALLOW_SEALING)
    try:
        os.ftruncate(descriptor,max(1,len(initial)))
        at=0
        while at<len(initial):
            written=os.pwrite(descriptor,initial[at:],at)
            if written<=0:raise OSError('short shared output preimage write')
            at+=written
        fcntl.fcntl(descriptor,getattr(fcntl,'F_ADD_SEALS',1033),7)
        if fcntl.fcntl(descriptor,getattr(fcntl,'F_GET_SEALS',1034)) & 7 != 7:
            raise OSError('shared output extent sealing failed')
        yield descriptor
    finally:
        os.close(descriptor)

    data=bytearray()
    while len(data)<capacity:
        chunk=os.pread(descriptor,capacity-len(data),len(data))
        if not chunk:raise OSError('short shared output observation')
        data.extend(chunk)
    return bytes(data)

    # Validate before creating a file descriptor or serializing large buffers.
    frame(image_bytes,source,capacity,workspace_size,workspace_fill)
    initial = b'\xa5'*capacity if output_initial is None else output_initial
    if not isinstance(initial,bytes) or len(initial)!=capacity:
        raise ValueError('output preimage must match the capacity')
    with shared_output(initial,output_initial is not None or observe_trap_writes) as capture_fd:
        payload = frame(image_bytes,source,capacity,workspace_size,workspace_fill,capture_fd)
        input_path = directory/(label+'.input.bin')
        output_path = directory/(label+'.output.bin')
        input_path.write_bytes(source)
        request = {'format':image_format, 'transport':transport,
            'image':str(image.resolve()), 'image_sha256':digest(image_bytes),
            'source':str(input_path.resolve()), 'source_sha256':digest(source),
            'capacity':capacity, 'workspace_size':workspace_size, 'workspace_fill':workspace_fill,
            'observer_sha256':digest(executable),'shared_output_fd':capture_fd,
            'observe_trap_writes':observe_trap_writes,'output_initial_sha256':digest(initial), 'frame_sha256':digest(payload),
            'output':str(output_path.resolve())}
        (directory/(label+'.request.json')).write_text(json.dumps(request,sort_keys=True)+'\n')
        began = time.monotonic_ns()
        output = b''
        try:
            try:
                process = execute(executable,payload,cwd=directory,output_fd=capture_fd)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
                stderr = exc.stderr or b''
                if exc.stdout:
                    (directory/(label+'.failure-stdout.raw')).write_bytes(exc.stdout)
                result = {'status':'timeout','wall_limit_seconds':20}
            else:
                stderr = process.stderr
                if process.returncode:
                    if process.stdout:
                        (directory/(label+'.failure-stdout.raw')).write_bytes(process.stdout)
                    result = {'status':'child_failed','returncode':process.returncode,
                        'stderr':stderr.decode('utf-8','replace')[-4096:]}
                else:
                    raw = process.stdout
                    if len(raw) != 24+len(source)+capacity+workspace_size or raw[:8] != b'HIAOBR02' or stderr:
                        (directory/(label+'.failure-stdout.raw')).write_bytes(raw)
                        result = {'status':'protocol_failed','returncode':0,
                            'response_bytes':len(raw),'response_sha256':digest(raw),
                            'error':'native observer response framing differs'}
                    else:
                        returned, elapsed = struct.unpack_from('<2Q',raw,8)
                        actual_source = raw[24:24+len(source)]
                        output = raw[24+len(source):24+len(source)+capacity]
                        workspace = raw[24+len(source)+capacity:]
                        output_path.write_bytes(output)
                        if actual_source != source:
                            (directory/(label+'.modified-source.bin')).write_bytes(actual_source)
                        result = {'status':'returned','result_u64':returned,'abi_status':returned>>32,
                            'return_encoding':'zero-extended-u32','core_u32':returned & 0xffffffff,
                            'source_sha256':digest(source),'image_sha256':digest(image_bytes),
                            'output_sha256':digest(output),'source_unchanged':actual_source==source,
                            'output_unchanged':output==initial,
                            'workspace_header':{str(at):int.from_bytes(workspace[at:at+8],'little')
                                for at in WORKSPACE_FIELDS if workspace_size>=at+8},
                            'native_elapsed_ns':elapsed,'forbidden_compiler_modules_loaded':[],
                            'loader_operations':loader_operations,
                            'limits':{'cpu_seconds':10,'address_bytes':256<<20,'core_dumpable':False,
                                'stack_bytes':8<<20,'output_capacity':capacity,'workspace_bytes':workspace_size}}
        finally:
            capture=None
            if capture_fd is not None:
                capture=read_capture(capture_fd,capacity)
        if capture is not None and result.get('status')=='returned' and capture!=output:
            raise AssertionError('returned output differs from actual shared mapping')
        if observe_trap_writes:
            if capture is None or len(capture)!=capacity:
                raise AssertionError('shared output observation unavailable')
            output=capture
            output_path.write_bytes(output)
            result['shared_output_observation']={
                'available':True,'initial_sha256':digest(initial),'observed_sha256':digest(output),
                'observed_bytes':len(output),'unchanged':output==initial,
                'capture_origin':'parent-owned size-sealed memfd, mapped by actual native child'}
        result.update(case=label,input_sha256=digest(source),input_bytes=len(source),
            artifact_sha256=digest(image_bytes),format=image_format,runner_sha256=digest(executable),
            wall_elapsed_ns=time.monotonic_ns()-began,transport=request['transport'],
            fresh_native_exec=True,successor_process_reuse=False)
        if observer.read_bytes()!=executable or image.read_bytes()!=image_bytes or input_path.read_bytes()!=source:
            raise AssertionError('native observer or immutable inputs changed')
        (directory/(label+'.stdout.log')).write_text(json.dumps(result,sort_keys=True)+'\n')
        (directory/(label+'.stderr.log')).write_bytes(stderr)
        (directory/(label+'.receipt.json')).write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2,sort_keys=True)+'\n')
        return result, output

def build_seed(directory, source=None):
    """The explicit B0 trust boundary; never called for a later generation."""
    from hepta.hia_agent_assembly import assemble_program
    from hepta.hia_program_native import emit_program_machine, compile_program_machine
    source = SOURCE.read_bytes() if source is None else source
    checked = assemble_program(source)
    machine = emit_program_machine(checked, foreign_buffer_exports=(("f0", CAPACITY),))
    output = Path(directory) / "B0.so"
    receipt = compile_program_machine(machine, program=checked, output=output, linker="ld")
    receipt["source_sha256"] = digest(source)
    receipt["seed_only"] = True
    document = checked.as_dict()
    receipt["source_structure"] = {
        "functions": len(document["functions"]),
        "instructions": sum(len(block["ops"]) for fn in document["functions"] for block in fn["blocks"]),
        "blocks": sum(len(fn["blocks"]) for fn in document["functions"]),
        "backward_direct_calls": [
            {"caller": fn["name"], "callee": op["attrs"]["function"]}
            for fn in document["functions"] for block in fn["blocks"] for op in block["ops"]
            if op["op"] == "call" and int(op["attrs"]["function"][1:]) < int(fn["name"][1:])],
        "direct_tail_self_calls": [
            {"caller": fn["name"], "block": block["id"]}
            for fn in document["functions"] for block in fn["blocks"]
            if block["ops"] and block["ops"][-1]["op"] == "call"
            and block["ops"][-1]["attrs"]["function"] == fn["name"]
            and block["term"] == {"op": "ret", "values": [block["ops"][-1]["out"][0]["name"]]}],
    }
    receipt["support_contract_sha256"] = digest((ROOT / CONTRACT_PATH).read_bytes())
    receipt["python"] = {"path": str(Path(sys.executable).resolve()),
                         "sha256": digest(Path(sys.executable).read_bytes()),
                         "version": sys.version, "isolated": bool(sys.flags.isolated),
                         "no_site": bool(sys.flags.no_site)}
    module_files = {}
    for name, module in tuple(sys.modules.items()):
        if name == "hepta" or name.startswith("hepta."):
            path = Path(module.__file__).resolve()
            relative = path.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
            module_files[relative] = digest(path.read_bytes())
    receipt["loaded_seed_modules"] = module_files
    (Path(directory) / "B0.receipt.json").write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    return output, receipt

def mutate_compiler(source):
    """An explicit source edit to code generation, not a source translator.

    The wrapper reserves 80 bytes instead of 64 while retaining 16-byte stack
    alignment. M1 still has its predecessor's 64-byte outer wrapper; M2 acquires
    the changed wrapper and M3 must reproduce M2 exactly.
    """
    contract = json.loads((ROOT / CONTRACT_PATH).read_text())
    wrapper = contract["compiler_symbols"]["mutation_wrapper"].encode("ascii")
    start = source.index(b"\nfn " + wrapper + b"(")
    end = source.index(b"\nend\n", start)
    section = source[start:end]
    old, new = b'{"value":64}', b'{"value":80}'
    assert section.count(old) == 1
    return source[:start] + section.replace(old, new) + source[end:]


def hash_reference(data):
    value = 5381

        "mutable-alias": sample.replace(b"b1(v0,v1,v2,v3,v4,v5)", b"b1(v0,v1,v1,v3,v4,v5)", 1),

            b'  v5:u32 = const() {"value":0}\n  ret(v5)\nend\n',
        "readonly-branch-alias": header + b'  v3:bool = const() {"value":false}\n'
            b"  branch v3 b1(v0,v0) b2()\nblock b1(v4:readbuf,v5:readbuf)\n"
            b'  v6:u32 = const() {"value":0}\n  ret(v6)\nblock b2()\n'
            b'  v7:u32 = const() {"value":0}\n  ret(v7)\nend\n',
        "readonly-write": sample.replace(b"  v20:u32 = call", b"  _ = buffer.store(v13,v16,v19)\n  v20:u32 = call", 1),
        "unreachable-block": sample.replace(b"end\nfn f1", extra + b"end\nfn f1", 1),
        "duplicate-function": sample.replace(b"fn f1(", b"fn f0(", 1),
        "quoted-declaration": sample.replace(b"fn f1(", b'fn "f1"(', 1),
        "unquoted-call": sample.replace(b'{"function":"f1"}', b'{"function":f1}', 1),
        "leading-zero": sample.replace(b'{"value":5381}', b'{"value":05381}', 1),
        "invalid-byte": sample + b"\x00",
        "empty-source": b"",
    }
    # These are required boundaries in the existing hia-asm.v1 regex grammar,
    # not just a preference for the renderer's whitespace spelling.
    spacing = {
        "function-adjacency": (b"fn f0(", b"fn f0 ("),
        "block-adjacency": (b"block b0(", b"block b0 ("),
        "effects-adjacency": (b"effects(", b"effects ("),
        "entry-adjacency": (b"entry(b0)", b"entry (b0)"),
        "entry-open-adjacency": (b"entry(b0)", b"entry( b0)"),
        "entry-close-adjacency": (b"entry(b0)", b"entry(b0 )"),

        "return-adjacency": (b"ret(v25)", b"ret (v25)"),
        "edge-adjacency": (b"jump b1(", b"jump b1 ("),
        "branch-separation": (b") b3(v7,v8,v10)", b")b3(v7,v8,v10)"),
        "opcode-adjacency": (b"buffer.len(v0)", b"buffer.len (v0)"),
        "constant-attribute-separation": (b"const() {", b"const(){"),
        "call-attribute-separation": (b"call(v17,v19) {", b"call(v17,v19){"),
        "cast-attribute-separation": (b"int.cast(v25) {", b"int.cast(v25){"),
        "effects-separation": (b"(u32) effects", b"(u32)effects"),
        "entry-separation": (b"trap) entry", b"trap)entry"),
    }
    for name, (old, new) in spacing.items():
        assert old in sample, name
        invalid[name] = sample.replace(old, new, 1)

def independent_call_reference(sample):
    """Record the general Core's distinct acceptance and scalar-execution view.

    Called before B0. The non-tail/mutual fixtures are legal general Core but
    refused by this native profile; never label that as Core invalidity.
    """
    from hepta.hia_agent_assembly import assemble_program
    from hepta.hia_program import HIAProgramRejected, execute_program
    backward = assemble_program(backward_bytesum_source(sample))
    chain = assemble_program(backward_chain_source())
    observations = []
    for left, right in ((0, 0), (5381, 255), (0xffffffff, 1), (0x80000000, 128)):
        observation = execute_program(backward, "f2", [left, right])
        assert observation["result"] == ((left * 33) ^ right) & 0xffffffff
        observations.append(observation)
    observation = execute_program(chain, "f127", [1], max_call_depth=128)
    assert observation["result"] == 127
    observations.append(observation)
    refusals = []
    for label, source in call_graph_invalid_sources(sample).items():
        try:
            assemble_program(source)
        except HIAProgramRejected as exc:
            refusals.append({"case": label, "source_sha256": digest(source),
                             "general_core": "rejected", "code": exc.code})
        else:
            raise AssertionError("invalid call source passed general Core: " + label)
    for label, source in recursion_refusals().items():
        checked = assemble_program(source)
        refusals.append({"case": label, "source_sha256": digest(source),
                         "general_core": "accepted", "core_sha256": checked.sha256,
                         "selfhost_profile_expected": "rejected: acyclic call graph required"})
    return {"general_core_observations": observations, "admission_differences": refusals}


def inspect_selfhost_object(data):
    """Read-only independent inspection; never constructs or repairs an object."""
    if len(data) < 64:
        raise ValueError("truncated HIA ELF object")
    header = struct.unpack_from("<16sHHIQQQIHHHHHH", data)
    ident, kind, machine, version, entry, phoff, shoff, flags, ehsize, phsize, phnum, shsize, shnum, names_index = header
    if (ident != b"\x7fELF\x02\x01\x01\x00" + b"\0" * 8
            or (kind, machine, version, entry, phoff, flags, ehsize, phsize, phnum, shsize, shnum, names_index)
            != (1, 62, 1, 0, 0, 0, 64, 0, 0, 64, 6, 4)
            or shoff % 8 or shoff + 6 * 64 != len(data)):
        raise ValueError("ELF header is outside the closed HIA ET_REL profile")
    sections = [struct.unpack_from("<IIQQQQIIQQ", data, shoff + i * 64) for i in range(6)]
    if any(sections[0]):
        raise ValueError("non-null ELF null section")
    for row in sections[1:]:
        if row[3] != 0 or row[4] < 64 or row[4] + row[5] > shoff:
            raise ValueError("ELF section outside the object payload")
    names = data[sections[4][4]:sections[4][4] + sections[4][5]]
    expected_names = b"\0.text\0.symtab\0.strtab\0.shstrtab\0.note.GNU-stack\0"
    if names != expected_names or [row[0] for row in sections] != [0, 1, 7, 15, 23, 33]:
        raise ValueError("ELF section-name inventory differs")
    text, sym, strings, shstrings, stack = sections[1:]
    if ((text[1], text[2], text[4], text[6], text[7], text[8], text[9]) != (1, 6, 64, 0, 0, 16, 0)
            or (sym[1], sym[2], sym[5], sym[6], sym[7], sym[8], sym[9]) != (2, 0, 72, 3, 2, 8, 24)
            or (strings[1], strings[2], strings[5], strings[6], strings[7], strings[8], strings[9]) != (3, 0, 4, 0, 0, 1, 0)
            or (shstrings[1], shstrings[2], shstrings[5], shstrings[6], shstrings[7], shstrings[8], shstrings[9]) != (3, 0, 49, 0, 0, 1, 0)
            or (stack[1], stack[2], stack[5], stack[6], stack[7], stack[8], stack[9]) != (1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0)):
        raise ValueError("ELF section flags or links differ")
    if (sym[4] != ((64 + text[5] + 7) & ~7) or strings[4] != sym[4] + 72
            or shstrings[4] != strings[4] + 4 or stack[4] != shstrings[4] + 49):
        raise ValueError("ELF payload layout differs")
    symbols = [struct.unpack_from("<IBBHQQ", data, sym[4] + i * 24) for i in range(3)]
    if (any(symbols[0]) or symbols[1] != (0, 3, 0, 1, 0, 0)
            or symbols[2][:5] != (1, 18, 0, 1, 0) or not 0 < symbols[2][5] <= text[5]
            or data[strings[4]:strings[4] + 4] != b"\0f0\0"):
        raise ValueError("ELF symbol inventory differs")
    return {"format": "ELF64-ET_REL", "machine": "EM_X86_64", "exports": ["f0"],
            "undefined_symbols": [], "external_relocations": [], "nonexecuting_stack_note": True,
            "text_offset": 64, "text_bytes": text[5], "text_sha256": digest(data[64:64 + text[5]]),
            "entry_wrapper_bytes": symbols[2][5], "object_sha256": digest(data)}


def observe_native_tool(directory, label, tool_name, arguments):
    path = shutil.which(tool_name)
    if path is None:
        raise RuntimeError("ELF qualification requires " + tool_name)
    path = Path(path).resolve()
    before = digest(path.read_bytes())
    command = [str(path), *map(str, arguments)]
    started = time.monotonic_ns()
    completed = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, timeout=20)
    (directory / (label + ".stdout.log")).write_bytes(completed.stdout)
    (directory / (label + ".stderr.log")).write_bytes(completed.stderr)
    receipt = {"command": command, "tool_sha256": before, "returncode": completed.returncode,
               "stdout_sha256": digest(completed.stdout), "stderr_sha256": digest(completed.stderr),
               "wall_elapsed_ns": time.monotonic_ns() - started}
    (directory / (label + ".command.json")).write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    if digest(path.read_bytes()) != before or completed.returncode:
        raise AssertionError({"native_tool_failed": label, "receipt": receipt})
    return receipt


def qualify_elf_outputs(directory, compilers, sample, checks):
    observations = []
    def object_source(source):
        return source.replace(b"hepta.hia.program.v8 selfhost\n",
                              b"hepta.hia.program.v8 selfhost_elf\n", 1)
    for label, compiler, own_source in compilers:
        for subject, source, flat in (("compiler", own_source, compiler),
                                     ("bytesum", sample, directory / (label + "-bytesum.image.bin"))):
            case = label + "-elf-" + subject
            obj, compilation = compile_stage(directory, case, compiler, object_source(source), output_extension=".o")
            inventory = inspect_selfhost_object(obj.read_bytes())
            checks[case + "_text_matches_flat"] = inventory["text_sha256"] == digest(flat.read_bytes())
            tools = [observe_native_tool(directory, case + "-readelf", "readelf", ["-W", "-h", "-S", "-s", "-r", obj]),
                     observe_native_tool(directory, case + "-objdump", "objdump", ["-d", "--disassemble=f0", obj])]
            linked = directory / (case + ".so")
            tools.append(observe_native_tool(directory, case + "-link", "ld",
                ["-m", "elf_x86_64", "-shared", "-z", "defs", "-z", "noexecstack",
                 "-z", "relro", "-z", "now", "--build-id=none", obj, "-o", linked]))
            checks[case + "_independent_tools_accept"] = all(row["returncode"] == 0 for row in tools)
            observations.append({"case": case, "compilation": compilation, "inventory": inventory,
                                 "tool_observations": tools, "linked_sha256": digest(linked.read_bytes())})
            if subject == "compiler":
                rebuilt, result = compile_stage(directory, case + "-rebuild", linked, own_source,
                                                 image_format="linked-selfhost")
                checks[case + "_linked_self_rebuild"] = rebuilt.read_bytes() == flat.read_bytes()
                observations.append(result)
            else:
                for index, data in enumerate((b"", bytes(range(256)) * 4)):
                    result, output = invoke(directory, case + "-run-" + str(index), linked, data,
                                            image_format="linked-selfhost", capacity=1, workspace_size=1)
                    checks[case + "_behavior_" + str(index)] = (result.get("status") == "returned"
                        and result.get("core_u32") == hash_reference(data) and result.get("source_unchanged")
                        and output == bytes([hash_reference(data) & 255]))
                    observations.append(result)
            result, _ = invoke(directory, case + "-short-output", compiler, object_source(source),
                               capacity=compilation["produced_bytes"] - 1)
            checks[case + "_short_output_transactional"] = (result.get("status") == "returned"
                and result.get("core_u32") == NO_SPACE and result.get("output_unchanged"))
            observations.append(result)
        rejected = {"bad-call": call_graph_invalid_sources(sample)["backward-signature"],
                    "recursive": recursion_refusals()["mutual-recursion"]}
        for name, bad in rejected.items():
            result, _ = invoke(directory, label + "-elf-reject-" + name, compiler, object_source(bad))
            checks[label + "_elf_reject_" + name] = (result.get("status") == "returned"
                and result.get("core_u32") == INVALID and result.get("output_unchanged")
                and result.get("source_unchanged"))
            observations.append(result)
    return observations


def _phase_manifest_digest(manifest):
    return digest(json.dumps(manifest, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode())


def _phase_inputs(directory, family, compiler, label):
    paths = {"native_observer": directory / "native-observer.elf",
             "linked_observer": directory / "linked-observer.elf",
             "compiler": compiler, "source": SOURCE, "sample": SAMPLE,
             "modified_source": directory / "modified-selfhost.hiaasm"}
    if family in PHASE_REFERENCE_FILES:
        paths["reference"] = directory / PHASE_REFERENCE_FILES[family]
    if family == "elf":
        paths["sample_image"] = directory / (label + "-bytesum.image.bin")
    return {name: {"path": str(Path(path).resolve()), "sha256": digest(Path(path).read_bytes())}
            for name, path in paths.items()}


def _read_phase_inputs(inputs):
    result = {}
    for name, identity in inputs.items():
        data = Path(identity["path"]).read_bytes()
        if digest(data) != identity["sha256"]:
            raise ValueError("qualification phase input changed: " + name)
        result[name] = data
    return result

            "checks": checks, "observations": observations,

            "worker_pid": os.getpid(),
            "python": {"isolated": bool(sys.flags.isolated), "no_site": bool(sys.flags.no_site),
                       "dont_write_bytecode": bool(sys.flags.dont_write_bytecode)},
            "fresh_host_oracle_process": True, "successor_process_reuse": False}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _PendingPhaseArchive:
    future: object


class _PhaseArchivePool:
    """One archiver, at most two unsealed completed phases, no native calls.

    Holding an oracle slot while archiving a stopped child unnecessarily
    serializes native work behind filesystem/compression work. The separate
    bounded lane retains every byte and all seal/replay checks. Its queue can
    add at most two phase directories to the two currently executing phases;
    a phase is not completed in the index until its archive succeeds.
    """
    def __init__(self):
        self._slots = BoundedSemaphore(2)
        self._pool = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1, thread_name_prefix="hia-stage-archive")

    def __enter__(self):
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exception):
        self._pool.shutdown(wait=True)

    def submit(self, function, *arguments):
        self._slots.acquire()
        try:
            future = self._pool.submit(function, *arguments)
        except BaseException:
            self._slots.release()
            raise
        future.add_done_callback(lambda completed: self._slots.release())
        return _PendingPhaseArchive(future)


def _seal_qualification_phase(phase_directory, archive_token, receipt_path, report, receipt):
    from tools.hia_evidence_archive import archive_completed_stage
    receipt["raw_artifacts"] = archive_completed_stage(phase_directory, archive_token)
    receipt["archive_completed_monotonic_ns"] = time.monotonic_ns()
    receipt_path.write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    return report, receipt


def _run_qualification_phase(directory, family, label, compiler, manifest_digest, archives=None):
    stem = "phase-" + family + "-" + label
    phase_directory = directory / "phase-runs" / (family + "-" + label)
    phase_directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False, mode=0o700)
    # Only this newly constructed stage may be losslessly packed after its
    # direct worker exits. Existing/frozen evidence is never swept or mutated.
    import secrets
    from tools.hia_evidence_archive import OWNER
    archive_token = secrets.token_hex(32)
    (phase_directory / OWNER).write_text(archive_token)
    request = {"schema": "hepta.hia.selfhost-phase-request.v1", "family": family,
               "compiler_label": label, "directory": str(phase_directory),
               "inputs": _phase_inputs(directory, family, compiler, label),
               "source_manifest_sha256": manifest_digest}
    request_path, report_path = directory / (stem + ".request.json"), directory / (stem + ".json")
    request_path.write_text(json.dumps(request, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    command = [sys.executable, "-I", "-S", "-B", str(Path(__file__).resolve()),
               "--phase-request", str(request_path), "--output", str(report_path)]
    started = time.monotonic_ns()
    with (directory / (stem + ".stdout.log")).open("wb") as stdout, (directory / (stem + ".stderr.log")).open("wb") as stderr:
        # At most two host-oracle workers run concurrently. Their native calls
        # remain individual resource-limited children. Flat and linked HIA ABI
        # calls exec sealed HIA-emitted observers without a Python child runtime;
        # linked targets still traverse the actual complete shared-object loader.
        with subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=phase_directory, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                              stdout=stdout, stderr=stderr) as process:
            returncode = process.wait()
            worker_pid = process.pid
    receipt = {"schema": "hepta.hia.selfhost-phase-process.v1", "family": family,
               "compiler_label": label, "command": command, "returncode": returncode,
               "worker_pid": worker_pid, "started_monotonic_ns": started,
               "completed_monotonic_ns": time.monotonic_ns(),
               "wall_elapsed_ns": time.monotonic_ns() - started,
               "report_sha256": digest(report_path.read_bytes()) if report_path.exists() else None}
    (directory / (stem + ".process.json")).write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    if returncode or not report_path.exists():
        raise AssertionError({"qualification_phase_failed": stem, "receipt": receipt})
    report = json.loads(report_path.read_text())
    _read_phase_inputs(request["inputs"])
    if (report.get("schema") != "hepta.hia.selfhost-phase.v1"
            or report.get("family") != family or report.get("compiler_label") != label
            or report.get("worker_pid") != worker_pid
            or report.get("source_manifest_sha256") != manifest_digest
            or report.get("input_sha256") != {key: value["sha256"] for key, value in request["inputs"].items()}
            or report.get("python") != {"isolated": True, "no_site": True, "dont_write_bytecode": True}
            or report.get("fresh_host_oracle_process") is not True
            or report.get("successor_process_reuse") is not False):
        raise AssertionError("qualification phase receipt identity differs: " + stem)
    arguments = (phase_directory, archive_token, directory / (stem + ".process.json"), report, receipt)
    if archives is not None:
        return archives.submit(_seal_qualification_phase, *arguments)
    return _seal_qualification_phase(*arguments)


def _merge_qualification_phases(results, checks):
    expected = {(family, label) for family in QUALIFICATION_FAMILIES for label in ("original", "modified")}
    if len(results) != len(expected):
        raise AssertionError("incomplete qualification phase inventory")
    phases, pending_checks = {}, {}
    for report, receipt in results:
        key = report["family"], report["compiler_label"]
        if key not in expected or key in phases or type(report.get("checks")) is not dict or not report["checks"]:
            raise AssertionError("duplicate, unknown or empty qualification phase")
        if any(type(value) is not bool for value in report["checks"].values()):
            raise AssertionError("qualification phase checks must be booleans")
        if report.get("status") != ("PASS" if all(report["checks"].values()) else "FAIL"):
            raise AssertionError("qualification phase status differs from checks")
        if set(report["checks"]) & (set(checks) | set(pending_checks)):
            raise AssertionError("qualification phase would overwrite an existing check")
        pending_checks.update(report["checks"])
        phases[key] = (report, receipt)
    checks.update(pending_checks)
    return phases


def _collect_qualification_phases(directory, scheduled):
    """Observe every future, retaining all failures before refusing the batch."""
    index_path = directory / "phase-index.json"
    entries = [{"family": family, "compiler_label": label, "state": "pending",
                "request": str(directory / ("phase-" + family + "-" + label + ".request.json")),
                "report": str(directory / ("phase-" + family + "-" + label + ".json")),
                "process_receipt": str(directory / ("phase-" + family + "-" + label + ".process.json"))}
               for family, label, _ in scheduled]
    order = {future: position for position, (_, _, future) in enumerate(scheduled)}
    observed = set(order)
    results, failures, control_exceptions = {}, [], []

    def retain():
        value = {"schema": "hepta.hia.selfhost-phase-index.v1", "phases": entries,
                 "completed": sum(row["state"] != "pending" for row in entries),
                 "exceptions": len(failures)}
        temporary = index_path.with_suffix(".json.tmp")
        temporary.write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
        temporary.replace(index_path)

    retain()
    while order:
        done, _ = wait(order, return_when=FIRST_COMPLETED)
        for future in done:
            position = order.pop(future)
            entry = entries[position]
            try:
                result = future.result()
                if type(result) is _PendingPhaseArchive:
                    if result.future in observed:
                        raise AssertionError("qualification archive future reused")
                    observed.add(result.future)
                    order[result.future] = position
                    # The actual native work has ended, but raw evidence is
                    # not sealed yet. Keep the same pending index entry.
                    continue
            except BaseException as error:
                # Worker/seal exceptions are data until all known futures
                # have been observed. Control exceptions remain exceptions.
                entry.update(state="exception", exception_type=type(error).__module__ + "." + type(error).__qualname__,
                             exception_message=str(error))
                failures.append(entry.copy())
                if not isinstance(error, Exception):
                    control_exceptions.append(error)
            else:
                results[position] = result
                entry.update(state="completed", report_status=result[0].get("status"))
            retain()
    if control_exceptions:
        raise control_exceptions[0]
    if failures:
        raise AssertionError({"qualification_phase_exceptions": failures, "phase_index": str(index_path)})
    return [results[position] for position in range(len(scheduled))]

        digest(linked_observer.read_bytes()) == linked_observer_build['executable_sha256']
        and all(row['returncode'] == 0 for row in linked_observer_build['native_tool_observations']))
    observations = []
    for label, compiler in (("original", original), ("modified", previous)):
        executable, compilation = compile_stage(directory, label + "-bytesum", compiler, sample)
        observations.append(compilation)
        for index, data in enumerate((b"", b"HIA native bootstrap", bytes(range(256)) * 4)):
            result, raw = invoke(directory, label + "-sample-" + str(index), executable, data, capacity=1, workspace_size=1)
            correct = result.get("status") == "returned" and result.get("core_u32") == hash_reference(data) and raw == bytes([hash_reference(data) & 255]) and result.get("source_unchanged")
            checks[label + "_behavior_" + str(index)] = bool(correct)
            observations.append(result)
    rejected = []
    for label, bad in invalid_sources(sample).items():
        result, raw = invoke(directory, "reject-" + label, original, bad)
        good = result.get("status") == "returned" and result.get("core_u32") == INVALID and result.get("output_unchanged") and result.get("source_unchanged")
        checks["reject_" + label] = bool(good)
        rejected.append(result)
    readonly_image, readonly_build = compile_stage(directory, "readonly-call-code", original, readonly_call_source())

        executable, compilation = compile_stage(directory, label + "-full-call-depth",
                                                compiler, backward_chain_source())

        result, _ = invoke(directory, label + "-full-call-depth-run", executable, b"",
                           capacity=0, workspace_size=0)
        checks[label + "_128_function_backward_chain"] = (
            result.get("status") == "returned" and result.get("core_u32") == 127)
        call_observations.append(result)
        for case, bad in {**call_graph_invalid_sources(sample), **recursion_refusals()}.items():

            checks[label + "_reject_" + case] = (result.get("status") == "returned"

                and result.get("source_unchanged"))

    small, _ = invoke(directory, "short-output", original, source, capacity=stages[2]["produced_bytes"] - 1)

            scheduled = [(family, label, pool.submit(_run_qualification_phase, directory, family, label, compiler, manifest_digest, archives))
                         for family in QUALIFICATION_FAMILIES
                         for label, compiler in (("original", original), ("modified", previous))]
            phase_results = _collect_qualification_phases(directory, scheduled)
    phases = _merge_qualification_phases(phase_results, checks)

    def phase_observations(family):

    tail_observations = phase_observations("tail")
    select_observations = phase_observations("select")
    effect_observations = phase_observations("effects")
    multi_observations = phase_observations("multi")
    keyword_observations = phase_observations("keyword")

        "target": contract["target"], "abi": contract["abi"],
        "support_contract": {"path": CONTRACT_PATH, "sha256": before[CONTRACT_PATH]},
        "checkout": checkout_identity(),
        "source_manifest": before, "source_bytes": len(source), "source_sha256": digest(source),
        "checks": checks, "seed": seed_receipt, "generations": stages,

        "behavior_observations": observations, "rejection_observations": rejected,
        "readonly_call_observations": [readonly_build, readonly],
        "call_graph_observations": call_observations, "independent_core_reference": independent,
        "elf_object_observations": elf_observations,

        "loan_observations": loan_observations, "independent_loan_reference": loan_reference,

        "owned_elf_observations": owned_observations,

        "resource_observations": resource_observations, "independent_resource_reference": resource_reference,
        "expanded_capacity_observations": expanded_capacity, "independent_capacity_reference": capacity_reference,
        "tail_call_observations": tail_observations, "independent_tail_reference": tail_reference,
        "select_observations": select_observations, "independent_select_reference": select_reference,

        "capacity_observations": [small, workspace], "elapsed_ns": time.monotonic_ns() - started,

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--phase-request", type=Path)
    arguments = parser.parse_args()
    if arguments.phase_request is not None:
        report = qualification_phase(arguments.phase_request)
        arguments.output.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
        print(json.dumps({"status": report["status"], "family": report["family"],
                          "compiler_label": report["compiler_label"],
                          "checks_passed": sum(report["checks"].values()), "checks_total": len(report["checks"])}))
        return
    report = qualify(arguments.output)
    print(json.dumps({"status": report["status"], "output": str(arguments.output),
                      "checks_passed": sum(report["checks"].values()), "checks_total": len(report["checks"]),
                      "generation_sha256": [x["produced_sha256"] for x in report["generations"]],
                      "modified_generation_sha256": [x["produced_sha256"] for x in report["modified_generations"]]}, sort_keys=True))
    raise SystemExit(0 if report["status"] == "SELF_HOSTED_FIXED_CORE_PASS" else 1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
